summary: An actual sliced three-good, unit-speed, nonconical rank-two frame with quadratic last coordinate has Q(S) not contained in S, where Q is the first commutator with the original bad partial and S is the intrinsic leading kernel. The same Q is not locally nilpotent. A primitive normalizer criterion identifies the missing stability condition. Cone density restricts good-only changes, excludes good-only invariant rational functions, and gives an exact quadratic fixed-good shear criterion. The displayed counterexample is a recognized translation and its acceleration is removable, so shear-minimal stability and general rank-two recognition remain unsettled.

mathematical_boundary: The counterexample satisfies the actual supplied three-good, unit-speed, full constant span, speed-rank-two, nonconical and quadratic-last-coordinate premises. It disproves unconditional first-commutator preservation of the intrinsic plane, not recognition of the action.
The selected highest commutator is an LND in this example, while the first commutator is not. They cannot be interchanged in the rank-one content argument.
The normalizer criterion allows its scalar in A, not necessarily in S. Cone density forces good-only E-affine coordinate changes to be affine-linear and forces Frac(A) intersect Frac(Rgood) to be C.

A fixed-good shear removes nonzero quadratic acceleration exactly when it lies in the complex span of pairwise speed products. The displayed example is removable by V-Y squared, so it does not refute a stability theorem with an additional fixed-good-shear-minimality premise.
No new recognition theorem, shear-minimal counterexample, general rank-two closure, arbitrary-frame entry or unrestricted cancellation result is claimed.
